clue.text: Large blade with phoney coating's a cracker

indicators.note: the phoney person coats the large blade, wrapping round it on both sides

parts.note: a phoney is a shammer, one who shams
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
an edge is the cutting blade of a knife or tool

explanation.surface: A big knife disguised with a fake covering is said to be a real cracker.
explanation.definitionFit: A sledgehammer is a heavy tool used for cracking and smashing stone, so it is literally something that cracks.

clue.text: See 7
Accredited goal secures championship

indicators.note: the goal holds the championship firmly inside it, as if securing it

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
a title is a championship won in sport

explanation.surface: A winning goal clinches the title for an officially recognised team.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone entitled has been granted a right or qualification, just as an accredited person has official authorisation.

clue.text: Board agree to progress

definitions.meaning: first meaning: climb aboard a bus or train
second meaning: be on friendly terms with someone

explanation.surface: A company's directors consent to moving forward with a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers boarding a vehicle, getting along with people, and advancing in life.

clue.text: Transmissions from an English port in case of hostilities

indicators.note: the words an English port go inside the casing formed by the other word
the case of a word is its outer shell, here the first and last letters of hostilities

parts.note: Dover is the English Channel port in Kent

explanation.surface: Broadcasts are sent from a Kentish harbour in the event of war.
explanation.definitionFit: Handovers are transfers of something from one party to another, a sense of transmission as passing on.

clue.text: Every seven days, leader apparently turned up submissively

indicators.note: the first letter is flipped upside down, as it looks in a down entry: a W inverted resembles an M

parts.note: weekly means once every seven days

explanation.surface: Each week the boss obediently appeared, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: Turn the W at the head of WEEKLY upside down and it looks like an M; 'apparently' admits this is a visual trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Meekly describes acting in a quiet, docile, unresisting way, which is what submissively means.

clue.text: What remains of passion and honour in hero's heart

indicators.note: the honour sits inside the core of the hero
the heart of a word is its middle, here the central pair of letters

parts.note: the hero, whose middle letters are taken
the MBE (Member of the Order of the British Empire) is a British honour

explanation.surface: Of a hero's love and decoration, little is left at his core.
explanation.walkthrough: The MBE (Member of the Order of the British Empire) is a British award, a stock crossword honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A dying ember is the glowing remnant of a fire, and figuratively the last trace of an old passion.

clue.text: Engineer can request a book, needing to start afresh, it's said

definitions.text: needing to start afresh, it's said

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or rework, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mechanic asks for a manual because the job must be restarted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' looks like a noun, but it is a verb telling you to rearrange CAN REQUEST A BOOK, all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means returning to the very beginning after a setback, so you have to start all over again.

clue.text: Former European politician with time to spare

explanation.surface: An ex-MEP now has free time on their hands.
explanation.definitionFit: To exempt someone is to free them from a duty, which is to spare them it.

clue.text: Mature lawyer retired last month

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the lawyer is read backwards

parts.note: ult., short for ultimo, means last month in formal letters

explanation.surface: A grown-up attorney stepped down a month ago.
explanation.walkthrough: ULT (ultimo) is old business-letter shorthand for 'of last month'.
explanation.definitionFit: An adult is a fully grown, mature person; both words describe someone past childhood.

clue.text: Modified Bronx diet, one with lighter content

indicators.note: a modified diet is altered, so the letters of Bronx diet are rearranged

explanation.surface: A New York eating plan is changed to include something less calorific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lighter content' suggests a low-calorie diet, but it means the tools for making fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinderbox held flint, steel and tinder, the kit for kindling a flame, so its contents were a fire-lighter.

clue.text: Work colleague conclusively classifying short fibrous protein

indicators.note: taking each word at its conclusion, its final letter
the word is cut short, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A co-worker ends up categorising a stringy body protein.
explanation.definitionFit: Keratin is the structural protein making up hair, nails and horn, and it forms fibres.

clue.text: Barrel transporting vintage spirit across island

indicators.note: the vintage spirit carries the island within it

explanation.surface: A cask of aged liquor is shipped over to an island.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil drum is a large metal barrel used for storing and shipping oil.

clue.text: Vigilant dancing in Swan Lake?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: alert and ready, an idiom
second meaning: literally, ballerinas dance on the tips of their toes (en pointe)

explanation.walkthrough: Swan Lake is Tchaikovsky's ballet, so the question mark points to dancers on pointe.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means alert and ready to act, while ballet dancers literally balance on their toe tips.

clue.text: Like canine amputee in yard?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a dog that has lost a leg has only three of its feet
second meaning: a yard measures exactly this length

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'yard' is the unit of length, not a garden where a dog might be.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-legged dog walks on a trio of paws, and a yard is the length of a trio of foot measures.

clue.text: Correct last of errors in project

indicators.note: the final letter sits inside the word for project

parts.note: to jut is to project or stick out

indicators.note: only the final letter of errors is used

explanation.surface: Fix the final mistake in the project.
explanation.definitionFit: Just can mean right or proper, as in a fair and correct decision.

clue.text: Horrid ugly things not good for recycling

indicators.note: the letter for good is left out of the pool before rearranging
recycled material is reprocessed into something new, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Nasty, unattractive items that are useless get sent for recycling.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsightly means ugly or unpleasant to look at, close to horrid in describing something offensive.

clue.text: Stammering man's just what's needed by worker

parts.note: he's, the contraction of he is
it means the very thing, as in 'that's it'

explanation.surface: A stuttering man is exactly what an employee requires.
explanation.walkthrough: The worker is the insect: the ant is the stock crossword worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitant speech falters and stops, as stammering speech does.

clue.text: Team from busy Cheshire station on the air

indicators.note: broadcast speech is heard, so the station name is spoken

parts.note: Crewe in Cheshire is a major railway junction

explanation.surface: Staff at a crowded railway station in north-west England go out on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: Crewe, in the English county of Cheshire, is a famous railway junction town.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew is a group of people working together, such as the staff of a ship or a film.

clue.text: Extraterrestrial's son's declining wits

indicators.note: in a down entry, declining means going lower, so the letter for son moves down to the bottom

parts.note: cosmic means from outer space, extraterrestrial
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: An alien's boy is losing his sense of humour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'declining' moves the S of COSMIC down to the end of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Comics are comedians, and a wit is a person who makes clever jokes.

clue.text: Revives female pen-pushers despatching first novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new arrangement
the opening letter is sent away

parts.note: the word with its first letter removed is the fodder

explanation.surface: A woman restores office clerks after sending away a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'despatching first' drops the P to leave ENPUSHERS, which 'novel' rearranges after F.
explanation.definitionFit: To freshen up is to refresh oneself, restoring energy and looking revived.

clue.text: Need university dons to write lines

indicators.note: to don is to put on, so the university is wrapped into the other pieces

parts.note: RY, railway, the lines a train runs on

explanation.surface: Academics require that university lecturers write lines.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface 'dons' are lecturers, but here it is a verb for putting on.
explanation.definitionFit: Penury is extreme poverty, a state of great need.

clue.text: Nutty Scottish leader once losing face

definitions.note: used adjectivally, as in almond flavour; an almond is a nut

indicators.note: the face of a word is its front letter, which is lost

parts.note: Alex Salmond was a former First Minister of Scotland

explanation.surface: A crazy former Scottish leader is humiliated.
explanation.walkthrough: Alex Salmond led the Scottish government as First Minister from 2007 to 2014.
explanation.definitionFit: An almond is a kind of nut, so almond-flavoured things taste nutty.

clue.text: Wine the French rejected drunk by agent

indicators.note: the agent swallows the other piece inside him

parts.note: a mole is a spy or secret agent

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the article is read backwards

explanation.surface: A spy downs a wine that French drinkers spurned.
explanation.definitionFit: Moselle is white wine from the Mosel valley of Germany and Luxembourg.

clue.text: Amateur in prison making way up

indicators.note: the letter for amateur is placed inside the prison word

explanation.surface: A novice in jail finds a route to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair, or flight of stairs, is the means of climbing to a higher floor.

clue.text: Not quite happening

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means approaching an age or time, and also taking place at present.

clue.text: Zest revolutionised hot sugary drinks

indicators.note: turned round, so the run of letters reads backwards
the phrase swallows the answer within it

explanation.surface: Revolutionary flair turned hot, sweet beverages upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty enjoyment and enthusiasm, the same eager energy as zest.

clue.text: Loud insistent call oddly tender

indicators.note: take the odd-numbered letters, first and third

explanation.surface: A loud, demanding cry is strangely affectionate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'insistent call' suggests the noun clamour, but 'call' is the fodder for 'oddly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Clamorous means making a noisy, vehement outcry, so it is both loud and insistent.

clue.text: Moving 23?

indicators.note: moving shifts one letter of the stair to a new spot

parts.note: the answer to 23 down, a stair

explanation.surface: A moving stair, like an escalator, is in motion.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: STAIR rearranged gives the word, and a moving stair is astir.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means in motion or active, as a moving staircase is.

clue.text: Acclaim luminary meriting advance

parts.note: a worthy is a notable, distinguished person

explanation.surface: Praise for a famous figure who deserves promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A creditworthy borrower is judged fit to receive a loan, which is an advance of money.
